root_idea.summary: The root centers on uncovering or removing what covers something.
root_idea.development: From uncovering and exposure, the lexical range extends to bare or cleared states, depletion and exhaustion, and grief or regret over something that has escaped.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Inflectional and vocative variant of حَسْرَة, appearing in يا حسرتنا.
Vocative variant of حَسْرَة, appearing in يا حسرتى.

senses.definition: To become weary or exhausted through exertion.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, Form X appears under negation and describes not becoming weary in sustained worship; the derived form gives an intensified sense of ordinary weariness.

senses.definition: Of the sight: exhausted, failing, or unable to achieve its object after prolonged looking.
senses.usage_conditions: In 67:4, the returning sight is described as حَسِير. The form permits an active interpretation, “failing,” and a passive interpretation, “made weary.”

senses.definition: Intense grief or regret over something missed, lost, or that has escaped one; lamentation over that loss.
senses.usage_conditions: The form occurs in singular and plural, and in vocative constructions such as يا حسرة, يا حسرتنا, and يا حسرتى. These grammatical and rhetorical variants retain the same lexical meaning.

senses.definition: Left exhausted of one's resources, with nothing remaining in one's possession; insolvent.
senses.usage_conditions: In 17:29, it describes a person who has spent so excessively that nothing remains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To uncover, remove, take off, or strip away something that covers another thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of removing coverings, clothing, or other concealing objects; the construction may use عن to mark what is uncovered from.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To peel a branch or remove its outer covering.
To sweep a house or chamber.
To exhaust someone's possessions by begging until nothing remains in his possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative object construction describing depletion through repeated asking and giving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tire, fatigue, or jade a person or beast; to drive a camel until it is exhausted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The classical usage especially describes fatigue caused by travel or exertion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sight or eye, to become dim, dull, failing, or weary through prolonged looking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes visual powers weakened by the length of the space observed or by long looking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, the sea, or a great river, to sink, recede, or withdraw so that what was beneath it becomes exposed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of water withdrawing from a shore or place; this is a specialized intransitive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grieve for or regret intensely a thing that has escaped one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prepositional construction عَلَيْهِ marks the object of grief or regret.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To despise, annoy, vex, or drive another away.
To cause another to experience grief or regret, especially intensely, over something lost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction derived from the branch of grief and regret.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of birds, to moult or shed feathers.
Of a people or party, to experience fatigue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive usage referring to a group becoming weary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For plumage, fur, or soft hair to fall off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of feathers, a camel's soft hair, or similar bodily covering falling away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To uncover oneself or sit with the head or face uncovered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or intransitive construction concerning removal of one's own covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become uncovered or stripped of what covered it; of darkness, to clear away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive form describes a covering, including darkness, withdrawing or disappearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tired, fatigued, jaded, or emaciated through travel or overexertion, especially of a beast or camel.
Grieving or regretting most intensely over something that has escaped one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person experiencing extreme grief or regret.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uncovered or bare, lacking a helmet, coat of mail, turban, or other defensive or head covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an uncovered person; in the plural, it can describe foot-soldiers without armor and, in an idiom, walls without ornamental crestings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person's inner or intrinsic character, natural disposition, or quality as revealed by examination; in one usage, the countenance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression كريم المحسر describes someone whose inner character proves noble when examined.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The face or countenance; in the plural, exposed parts of the body such as the face, arms, and legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural refers to bodily parts left exposed to view.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An elevated, open tract of land bare of herbage or trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a desert or other ground whose natural covering is absent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An instrument for sweeping; a broom or besom.
Despised, harassed, vexed, driven away, or treated as an outcast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported adjectival usage applied to a person or group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made to grieve or regret intensely, or left fatigued.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation connects the condition with being driven away or exhausted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Removed, put off, taken off, or stripped away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive participle describes something from which a covering has been removed.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit gives the fatigue meaning and explicitly relates it to the Quranic Form X usage.
The sight-related meaning is covered by the Quran-attested adjective sense.
The Quran-attested depleted-resources usage is represented under the public Quranic form.

cautions: In 67:4, حَسِير permits both an active reading, “failing,” and a passive reading, “made weary”; the public sense preserves both interpretations.
Lane's historical Quran citation conventions are not used to infer modern verse locations; Quran examples here use independently supplied QAC locations.
